ai_summary: Great Britain's total wind generation currently stands at 5.8 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output delivering 3.0 GW, which corresponds to 29.7% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This high proportion of renewable generation drives Scottish carbon intensity down to just 2 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide average of 193 gCO2/kWh. However, transmission boundary limitations between Scotland and southern demand centers prevent this abundant green electricity from being fully utilized. Consequently, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 15.0 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, racking up a constraint cost of about £494,569. To replace this constrained clean volume, an estimated 2,841,051 m3 of natural gas was burned elsewhere across the network, generating an additional 5,234 tonnes of CO2. Annualizing today's constraint expenditure indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of £181 million. Across Great Britain's annual electricity demand, this volume of curtailment increases everybody's invoice in the UK by an estimated £0.60/MWh in balancing charges, highlighting the persistent financial and environmental consequences of cross-border grid congestion.
